signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Strait of Hormuz Supply Shock
signals.text: NOK 1W avg +1.594% (n=2 pairs) versus EUR -0.546% (n=9 pairs) creates a dominant 2.140% G10 spread that anchors topside momentum heading into the Sydney open. Escalating maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, marked by multiple tanker strikes, reinforce crude premiums above $102.9/bbl and widen the terms-of-trade wedge against energy-importing Europe. The Sydney open provides the catalyst to price the weekend crude disruption directly into European cross rates. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/EUR into the weekly open; geopolitical energy disruption widens the structural outperformance gap. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open pricing weekend Strait of Hormuz escalation. Risk: Diplomatic de-escalation in the Persian Gulf collapsing crude risk premiums back below $100/bbl.
evidence: UKMTO/IRGC confirm multiple tanker strikes in Strait of Hormuz

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded COT Short Overhang + Fed Hawkish Divergence
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short of -94.1k contracts (33.6% long, 2nd percentile) anchors persistent downside pressure after EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1169. Hawkish commentary from Fed officials advocating multiple additional rate hikes combines with a +150bp SOFR-€STR carry advantage to suppress recovery attempts. The upcoming ECB meeting on 17 Dec and Fed meeting on 9 Dec serve as the policy drivers, but Friday's technical breakdown below the 20-day SMA leaves the pair vulnerable to further selling. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; heavy speculative shorting is sustained by widening policy and growth divergence. Catalyst: Sydney open follow-through on Fed hawkish comments. Risk: Short-covering squeeze triggered if spot reclaims the 20-day SMA at 1.1206.
evidence: SOFR vs €STR carry differential: +150bp favoring USD
Fed officials Daly, Musalem, and Logan signal further rate hikes needed

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded COT Long Exposure Ahead of RBA Decision
signals.text: AUD COT LF net long of +47.6k contracts (69.3% long) leaves the currency vulnerable to a crowded unwind after AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7035. While the RBA holds a +66bp OIS carry advantage over the Fed, Australia's negative ESI at -5.1 and an unemployment rate uptick to 4.7% challenge aggressive policy tightening expectations. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 77% hike priced) on 3 Nov is the catalyst that determines whether the hike bias can be sustained. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD into the RBA decision; stretched speculative length faces unwinding risk on policy hesitation. Catalyst: RBA policy decision on 3 Nov. Risk: RBA delivers a hawkish rate increase that validates long positioning above 0.7072 resistance.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Crowded Speculative Short Exposure + Geopolitical Oil Surge
signals.text: CAD COT LF net short of -92.8k contracts (17.6% long, 12th percentile) establishes significant short-squeeze risk following USD/CAD's Friday close at 1.3979. Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions pushing crude higher reinforce Canadian terms of trade, directly threatening USD/CAD despite the Fed's +170bp OIS carry premium. The next BoC meeting (mkt: 100% hike priced) on 9 Dec determines policy trajectory, but immediate price action hinges on energy flow repricing. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD into the open; extreme CAD short positioning collides with sharp crude oil upside. Catalyst: Energy market opening reaction to Iranian tanker incidents. Risk: USD/CAD pushes back above the 20-day SMA at 1.4137 if broad risk aversion triggers dollar funding demand.
evidence: Multiple tanker detonations confirmed in Strait of Hormuz
